title: response-contract-negotiator: add negotiation hints, soft-validation telemetry, and toolcall fencing for streaming
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: customers need a safer way to request structured output (JSON schema) in streaming scenarios while keeping OpenAI-compatible fallbacks. This PR implements a negotiation layer that surfaces validation hints in the response metadata, emits granular telemetry for validation failures, and ensures tool/function calls are fenced so partial JSON errors don't lead to unsafe executions.

What this does: adds a small response_contract negotiator that sits between the API surface and the runtime. The negotiator: 1) negotiates an effective response_format (strict|soft|hint-only) with explicit headers and an OpenAI-compatibility fallback, 2) exposes X-Response-Validation hint headers that the runtime uses to apply best-effort coercion during streaming, 3) attaches a validation error map to telemetry (validation.stage -> error.code -> token_offset) for classification, 4) wraps tool/function calls with a two-phase commit-like fencing: tool intents are buffered until a schema checkpoint confirms safe structure, 5) provides a streaming checkpoint API so client libraries can request a resume token when partial validation errors occur.

Backward compatibility: default behavior remains the same unless a caller opts into a response_format that requests schema negotiation. OpenAI compatibility mode (response_format=openai_compat) maps the negotiator to a 'soft' mode that attempts best-effort coercion and surface a single top-level meta error rather than failing the stream.

Checklist:
- [x] core negotiator implementation in runtime/response layer
- [x] hint header + proto definitions and JS/Go SDK plumbing
- [x] integration tests for streaming resume and toolcall fencing
- [x] docs and API examples for response_format and OpenAI mapping
- [x] telemetry events, dashboard query and alert for validation regressions

Related: linear ENG-7842 (response contract telemetry), ENG-7990 (toolcall safety). Also references design notes: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-7842/response-contract-telemetry and internal RFC: /docs/rfc/response-negotiator.md

Notes for reviewers: the negotiator is intentionally conservative with changes to execution: it only changes toolcall timing when schema checkpoints are present, and it never suppresses user-visible content unless strict mode is selected. The PR contains a short shim in the OpenAI compatibility adapter so SDKs that set the old openai response_mode get mapped to response_format=openai_compat.

release_notes: Adds a response negotiation layer to enable JSON-schema-aware response_format options (strict / soft / hint-only), exposes validation hints for runtime coercion, implements toolcall fencing to avoid unsafe tool execution on malformed streams, and emits detailed validation telemetry for alerting and quality regression detection.
